stem: When a health care facility implements extended use of N95 respirators as a supply-conservation strategy, what does 'extended use' mean?

options.A: The same N95 is worn for repeated close-contact encounters with several patients without removing it between encounters
options.B: The same N95 is removed after each encounter, stored, and later donned again by the same worker
options.C: An N95 is shared between multiple health care workers during the same shift
options.D: A disposable N95 is worn indefinitely even after it becomes soiled or contaminated

rationale: Current NIOSH/CDC guidance defines extended use as wearing the same N95 respirator for repeated close-contact encounters with several different patients without removing the respirator between encounters. B describes limited reuse, which involves doffing and later redonning the respirator. Respirators should not be shared, and contaminated or otherwise unsuitable respirators should be discarded.
educational_objective: Distinguish extended use of an N95 respirator from limited reuse and unsafe sharing or continued use of a contaminated respirator.
source_organization: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), CDC
source_document_title: Strategies for Conserving the Supply of N95 Filtering Facepiece Respirators
source_locator: Extended use of N95 respirators as respiratory protection: definition; Limited re-use of N95 and other disposable respirators: reuse requires removal/donning between encounters; discard criteria
source_claim_supported: Extended use means wearing the same N95 for repeated patient encounters without removal between encounters; this differs from limited reuse, in which the respirator is doffed and redonned.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

correction_summary: Corrected the outdated classification of extended use as inherently a crisis-capacity strategy. Current NIOSH guidance permits extended use as a contingency-capacity strategy when appropriate. Reframed the item around the stable definition and distinction from limited reuse.
audit_findings: A exactly matches current NIOSH terminology. B is limited reuse; C violates individual-use principles; D contradicts discard criteria. No second-answer ambiguity, cueing, or outdated capacity-level claim remains.
